pages.lesson:
LESSON: WRITING 7.4.1 MECHANICS OF WRITING: PUNCTUATION

Grade: Grade 5
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
Strand: Strand 7
Topic 7.4: Writing 7.4.1 Mechanics of Writing: Punctuation

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Writing 7.4.1 Mechanics of Writing: Punctuation. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: Which punctuation marks do you know?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify commas and double quotation marks in written texts
2. use the comma and double quotation marks correctly in sentences

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: WRITING 7.4.1 MECHANICS OF WRITING: PUNCTUATION
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE · Grade: Grade 5
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Writing 7.4.1 Mechanics of Writing: Punctuation helps you succeed in ENGLISH LANGUAGE. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: WRITING 7.4.1 MECHANICS OF WRITING: PUNCTUATION
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Identify commas and double quotation marks in written texts

What this means
In this part you learn to identify commas and double quotation marks in written texts. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: identify commas and double quotation marks in written texts.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Writing 7.4.1 Mechanics of Writing: Punctuation”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can identify commas and double quotation marks in written texts. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Use the comma and double quotation marks correctly in sentences

What this means
In this part you learn to use the comma and double quotation marks correctly in sentences. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: use the comma and double quotation marks correctly in sentences.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model speaking: Say 4 clear sentences about Writing 7.4.1 Mechanics of Writing: Punctuation to a partner.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can use the comma and double quotation marks correctly in sentences. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Writing 7.4.1 Mechanics of Writing: Punctuation is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Writing 7.4.1 Mechanics of Writing: Punctuation”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: identify commas and double quotation marks in written texts)

Example 2: Say 4 clear sentences about Writing 7.4.1 Mechanics of Writing: Punctuation to a partner. (skill: use the comma and double quotation marks correctly in sentences)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Writing 7.4.1 Mechanics of Writing: Punctuation to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: identify commas and double quotation marks in written texts.
3. Practise this skill: use the comma and double quotation marks correctly in sentences.
4. Make one local Kenya example of Writing 7.4.1 Mechanics of Writing: Punctuation from your county, market, farm, or school.
5. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Writing 7.4.1 Mechanics of Writing: Punctuation: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 5 learner study Writing 7.4.1 Mechanics of Writing: Punctuation?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. Which punctuation marks do you know?
2. Why do we punctuate sentences?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Writing 7.4.1 Mechanics of Writing: Punctuation means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: identify commas and double quotation marks in written texts.
5. Be able to: use the comma and double quotation marks correctly in sentences.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
